TITLE: Second-Order Derivative Estimation via Weighted Average of Neural Tangent Kernels
PROPOSAL: We propose a new estimator for the second-order derivatives of a score function, an MLP model trained via denoising diffusion models, by averaging weighted neural tangent kernels (NTKs) at different initialization points. We leverage the unique linearity of NTKs and the fact that a weighted average of linear functions is linear, to reduce the variance of the curvature estimation while maintaining the same bias, hence approximating the true second-order derivatives more accurately.
CONTROLS: A baseline comparison with the second-order Stein gradient estimator used in DiffAN.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method should improve over DiffAN in terms of variance reduction with the same level of bias, outperforming it in low to mild curvature settings. However, the cumulative effect from initially high curvature regimes may negatively impact overall performance, mainly in high-dimensional settings.

CONTROLS: Analyze how the choice of initialization affects the performance of Proposal 1 by exploring other initialization schemes like those used in diffused-based models or unregularized models.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (to re-run Proposal 1 with different initializations)
PREDICTION: Using a stable initialization should improve the overall performance of Proposal 1, especially for small number of samples. However, large number of variables might still cause aggressive learning for the wrong directions in proposal 1 because a small amount of information is lost into the other set, potentially when converting sequences learned by score models with multiple intern repetitions.

TITLE: Score Model Simplification via Information-Theoretic Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose simplifying the score model used in score-matching-based causal ordering methods by adding an information-theoretic regularization term to the loss function, which encourages the score model to be more interpretable and easier to optimize. This regularization term can be based on metrics such as mutual information between the input and output of the score model.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of score models regularized with different information-theoretic metrics, and evaluate their impact on the overall accuracy of the causal ordering method.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (to re-run score model training with regularization)
PREDICTION: Our method should improve the interpretability and optimization of score models, reducing the risk of overfitting and improving the accuracy of causal ordering. However, the choice of regularization metric may affect the trade-off between interpretability and accuracy.

PROPOSAL: We propose using active learning to select the most informative samples for the causal ordering method, which can significantly reduce the number of required samples and improve the accuracy of the method. This is particularly important for high-dimensional causal discovery tasks, where collecting data can be expensive and time-consuming.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of active learning-based causal ordering in various high-dimensional settings, and compare it with random sampling and other active learning strategies.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Improved Second-Order Stein Gradient Estimator with Tensorized Kernel Approximations
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel second-order Stein gradient estimator with improved computational efficiency and reduced numerical instability by using tensorized kernel approximations. This will involve factorizing the kernel matrix into smaller components to enable efficient matrix operations and stabilize the estimator.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on synthetic datasets generated under both linear and nonlinear additive noise models, comparing with existing estimators like SCORE and CaPS. (2) Assess the effect of tensor rank, kernel choice, and sample size on performance. (3) Compare with DiffAN to gauge the impact of improved second-order derivative estimation.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This estimator is expected to outperform existing approaches, particularly in large-scale settings, by 20% in terms of mean absolute error, but may struggle with accurately capturing complex nonlinear relationships.

PROPOSAL: Enhance the tensorized kernel approximation approach by incorporating POSIX partitions in the factorization process. This can lead to further computational efficiency gains and improved stability in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: (1) Theoretical analysis on the benefits of POSIX partitions in terms of accuracy and computational cost. (2) Evaluation on synthetic datasets to compare with existing estimators, including the revised estimator without POSIX partitions. (3) Assess the impact of partition size and number on performance.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (accounts for additional partitioning computations)
PREDICTION: This improvement is expected to enhance the performance of the revised estimator by an additional 10% in terms of mean absolute error, especially in complex high-dimensional scenarios, but may introduce a small overhead due to the partitioning process.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Diffusion-SCORE: Combining Denoising Diffusion Models and Second-Order Stein Gradient Estimation for Improved Causal Ordering
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel approach, Diffusion-SCORE, that leverages the strengths of denoising diffusion models and second-order Stein gradient estimation. This method first trains a denoising diffusion model to estimate the score function, and then uses a second-order Stein gradient estimator with tensorized kernel approximations to accurately estimate Hessian diagonal entries.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on protein signaling networks and gene regulatory networks using synthetic datasets to compare with existing methods. (2) Assess the impact of the number of diffusion steps, kernel size, and tensor rank on performance. (3) Compare with DiffAN to gauge the effect of improved second-order derivative estimation.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to outperform existing methods by a significant margin, particularly in high-dimensional settings, with a potential 30% reduction in mean absolute error, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

(2) Assess the impact of attention mechanism design and hyperparameters on performance. (3) Compare with a baseline that uses a standard autoregressive prior.

title: stable approximate hessian diagonal with gans
PROPOSAL: We propose to combine the reliability of the Stein gradient estimator with the compactness and robustness of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). By employing a GAN to estimate the score function and its Hessian diagonal, we obtain a computationally and memory-efficient estimate that requires no second-order derivatives and can cope with high-dimensional settings. We suggest using a two-stream architecture where a normalizing flow is trained alongside the GAN to directly produce an unbiased estimate of the Hessian diagonal.
CONTROLS: Comparison with the second-order Stein gradient estimator and its variants, such as DiffAN.
COST: 10000 GPU-hours, to allow for extensive grid search and ablation experiments.
PREDICTION: Our method will show significant improvement in estimating the Hessian diagonal and predicting causal orderings under nonlinear ANM, while also demonstrating scalability and robustness to high-dimensional settings.
